brief: Goldman Sachs decomposes August's 0.7pp core PCE overshoot (3.0% vs its 2.3% forecast) to test whether it reflects fading one-off shocks or stickier underlying inflation. Consumer electronics add over 0.3pp from an AI-driven price boost, but GS argues roughly half of the software-and-accessories piece (0.2pp) is mismeasurement: the category is overweighted in PCE versus CPI and not quality-adjusted for AI features, overstating the true contribution by 0.1pp, and its fading memory-price shock should ease the component in 2027. Air transportation adds 0.2pp from jet-fuel costs tied to the Iran war. Broader energy passthrough contributes 0.3pp more. An updated model puts tariff passthrough at 80% versus 70% assumed in January, but a lower effective tariff rate after the Supreme Court's IEEPA ruling offsets most of that, leaving only 0.1pp net tariff surprise. Shelter adds 0.1pp on slower disinflation. Pharma and used-vehicle declines (Medicare negotiations, TrumpRx, patent expirations, a 2025 unwind) subtract 0.2pp and look durable. GS concludes the oil shock, tariffs and the software component explain roughly three-fourths of the surprise and should fade, leaving about 0.2pp of genuine upside (housing, AI electronics) without a meaningful acceleration in trend inflation. It still expects core PCE at 2.2% by December 2027.
